exEn: We need to think more about the environment.
note: Stress on the last syllable: mil-JÖ. It also means surroundings: arbetsmiljö = working environment.

ex: Tåget är ett {miljövänligt} sätt att resa.
exEn: The train is an eco-friendly way to travel.
The climate is getting warmer and warmer.
Climate change affects the whole world.
note: Usually plural in Swedish: klimatförändringarna = climate change.

exEn: We have to cut carbon dioxide emissions.
note: Same form in the plural: ett utsläpp, många utsläpp. From släppa ut (to let out).

exEn: Air pollution can cause asthma.
note: Mostly used in the plural. The verb is förorena (to pollute).

exEn: We use less energy in the summer.
note: Stress on the last syllable, and g before i sounds like sj: e-ner-SHEE.

exEn: Sweden is investing heavily in renewable energy.
note: The older word förnyelsebar means the same.

exEn: Solar energy is getting cheaper every year.

ex: Det byggs mycket {vindkraft} i norra Sverige.
exEn: A lot of wind power is being built in northern Sweden.
note: A wind turbine is ett vindkraftverk.

exEn: Coal and oil are fossil fuels.
note: fossila bränslen = fossil fuels.

exEn: We recycle glass, paper and plastic.
note: Irregular like vinna: återvann, återvunnit. The noun is återvinning (recycling).

ex: Det är {pant} på burkar och plastflaskor.
exEn: There's a deposit on cans and plastic bottles.
note: Usually 1 or 2 kronor. You get it back at the bottle machine in the supermarket (pantmaskinen).

exEn: I'm going to return the cans at the store.
note: The machine gives you a receipt (pantkvitto) that you use at the checkout.

ex: Hemma {sorterar} vi soporna i olika påsar.
exEn: At home we sort our trash into different bags.
note: Sorting household waste for recycling is called sopsortering or källsortering.

exEn: You can put food scraps in the compost.
note: Stress on the second syllable: kom-POST.

exEn: How do we build a sustainable society?
note: It also means durable: hållbara kläder. The noun is hållbarhet (sustainability).

exEn: I try to buy organic food.
note: Often shortened to eko: ekomjölk, ekobananer.

exEn: There was a lot of litter on the beach.
note: Also junk in general: Källaren är full av skräp.

ex: Det är förbjudet att {skräpa ner} i naturen.
exEn: It's forbidden to litter in nature.
note: Stress on ner. Also written skräpa ned.

ex: Det finns alldeles för mycket {plast} i haven.
exEn: There's far too much plastic in the oceans.
note: en plastpåse = a plastic bag.

exEn: Don't forget to rinse the packaging!
note: Packaging is recycled by material: plast, papper, glas or metall.

exEn: We shouldn't waste water.
note: Often slösa med: slösa med vatten, pengar, tid. The opposite is spara.

exEn: Turn off the light to save energy.
We have to protect the forest and the animals.
note: sk before y sounds like sj: SHYD-da. The noun is ett skydd (protection).

exEn: Many birds and insects are endangered.
note: utrotning (extinction) + hotad (threatened).

ex: {Allemansrätten} ger alla rätt att vara ute i naturen.
exEn: The right of public access gives everyone the right to be out in nature.
note: You may walk, camp for a night and pick berries almost anywhere. The rule: inte störa, inte förstöra (don't disturb, don't destroy). Always used in this definite form.

ex: Jag gillar {friluftsliv}, särskilt att vandra och fiska.
exEn: I like outdoor life, especially hiking and fishing.
note: A big part of Swedish life: spending free time out in nature, all year round.

exEn: Sarek is one of Sweden's national parks.
note: Sweden has about 30, from Abisko in the far north to Söderåsen in Skåne.

exEn: In the nature reserve, dogs must be on a leash.

ex: Långt upp i norr finns det mycket {vildmark}.
exEn: Far up north there's a lot of wilderness.

ex: Ön är känd för sitt rika {djurliv}.
exEn: The island is known for its rich wildlife.
note: dj- sounds like j: djur = YOOR.

exEn: Don't forget to water the plants!
note: From växa (to grow). A houseplant is en krukväxt.

ex: Vi ska vandra i {fjällen} i sommar.
exEn: We're going hiking in the mountains this summer.
note: fjällen = the bare mountains of northern and western Sweden, above the tree line. Berg is the general word for mountain.

exEn: We paddled a canoe on the river.
note: Used for the big rivers of northern Sweden, like Torne älv. Flod is mostly used for rivers abroad: Nilen är en flod.

exEn: Cloudberries grow on bogs up north.
note: Don't mix it up with myra (ant).

exEn: The glaciers melt as the climate gets warmer.
note: c before i sounds like s, and the stress is on the last syllable: gla-si-ÄR.

exEn: Kungsleden is Sweden's best-known hiking trail.
note: Often just leden: Följ leden! (Follow the trail!) Trails are marked with paint on trees and rocks.

exEn: Follow the path through the forest to the lake.
note: Also the imperative of stiga: Stig på! = Come in!

exEn: We slept in a tent by the lake.
note: The verb tälta means to camp in a tent.

ex: Ta med en varm {sovsäck}, nätterna är kalla.
exEn: Bring a warm sleeping bag, the nights are cold.

ex: Vi satt runt {elden} och grillade korv.
exEn: We sat around the fire and grilled sausages.
note: Eld is a fire you make, like in a fireplace; a fire that destroys a building is en brand. Göra upp eld = to make a fire.

exEn: We sang songs around the campfire.
Can you eat this mushroom?
note: It also means sponge. Many Swedes pick mushrooms in the autumn, especially kantareller (chanterelles).

exEn: We usually pick mushrooms in the autumn.
note: plocka upp = to pick up: Plocka upp ditt skräp!

exEn: The adder is Sweden's only venomous snake.
note: g before i sounds like j: YIF-tig. ett gift = a poison, but the adjective gift means married!

ex: Skogen är full av {bär} i augusti.
exEn: The forest is full of berries in August.
note: Same form in the plural: ett bär, två bär. Don't confuse it with bär (carries) from bära.

ex: Jag äter yoghurt med {blåbär} till frukost.
exEn: I have yogurt with blueberries for breakfast.
note: Wild Swedish blueberries (bilberries) are blue all the way through and stain your fingers.

ex: Vi äter köttbullar med potatis och {lingon}.
exEn: We're having meatballs with potatoes and lingonberries.
note: Usually eaten as lingonsylt (lingonberry jam) with meatballs, pancakes and much more.
